newsitem.title: SPAIN: Peseta ends weaker, BoS intervention rumoured.
newsitem.headline: Peseta ends weaker, BoS intervention rumoured.

text.p: The peseta finished weaker on Wednesday, but bounced off its weakest point amid talk the Bank of Spain had bought the peseta against the dollar, dealers said.
They added they believed the Bank of Spain had bought a small amount of pesetas at around 84.68/69 versus the mark.
The peseta ended its trading day at around 84.61/64 to the mark, having rebounded from 84.73.
In early dealings on Monday, it had traded at 84.12/14 and was at levels around 83.20 per mark last week. It was trading now at levels not seen since last August.
Dealers added that the mark has strong resistance at 84.60, and they added that if the German currency breaches that level, the next target would be founded at around 85.00.
